importantNotes: Romans has been called 'the cathedral of Christian faith' — the most influential theological letter ever written.
Romans 8 is considered one of the greatest chapters in the Bible — no condemnation, nothing separates us from God's love.
The 'Romans Road' (3:23, 6:23, 5:8, 10:9-10) is a classic gospel presentation.
Chapters 9-11 address God's plan for Israel — He has not rejected His people.
Martin Luther's study of Romans sparked the Protestant Reformation.

chapters.1: Paul's introduction and longing to visit Rome; the gospel's power; humanity's sinfulness.
chapters.2: God judges impartially; the Jews are not exempt from judgment; true circumcision is of the heart.
chapters.3: All have sinned; no one is righteous; justification is by faith, not by works of the law.
chapters.4: Abraham — the model of justification by faith; righteousness credited apart from works.
chapters.5: Peace with God through justification; suffering produces hope; Adam and Christ compared.
chapters.6: Dead to sin, alive in Christ; do not let sin reign; slaves of righteousness.
chapters.7: Released from the law; the struggle with sin — 'I do what I do not want to do.'
chapters.8: No condemnation in Christ; life in the Spirit; nothing can separate us from God's love.
chapters.9: God's sovereign choice — His mercy on whom He chooses; Israel's rejection of the gospel.
chapters.10: Salvation is for all who call on the name of the Lord; faith comes by hearing.
chapters.11: God has not rejected Israel; the olive tree analogy; all Israel will be saved; God's wisdom.
chapters.12: Living sacrifices; gifts of the body; love in action — bless those who persecute you.
chapters.13: Submit to authorities; love fulfills the law; put on the armor of light.
chapters.14: Do not judge others on disputable matters; the strong must bear with the weak.
chapters.15: Follow Christ's example of humility; Paul's mission to the Gentiles; travel plans.
chapters.16: Greetings to many individuals; warnings about divisive people; final doxology.
